Mia (Sales): @Arjun Claire's POC demo is intermittently failing — SSE starts, then client throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input`. Happens mostly on Chrome mobile behind their corporate proxy.

Arjun (SE): Can you paste the raw fragments and which SDK version they're using?

Claire (Client Eng): Raw from network tab (redacted):
```
data: {\"id\":\"x-11\",\"part\":\"{\\\"text\\\":\\\"Caf\"\n\n```
then next event:
```
data: {\"id\":\"x-11\",\"part\":\"\\u00e9 exp\\\"}\n\n```
They parse each `event.data` separately which fails when a multibyte char splits across messages. Using `@redwood/web-sdk@1.3.2` from CDN.

Arjun (SE): Likely causes: proxy adding gzip / re-chunking or older SDK not preserving incomplete UTF-8 across chunks. Short triage: 1) confirm `content-type: text/event-stream` and whether `content-encoding: gzip` is present, 2) reproduce with `curl -N -v` to see raw boundaries.

Claire (Client Eng): Confirmed: corporate proxy injects `content-encoding: gzip`. Reproduced locally by enabling gzip on a reverse proxy. Turning gzip off fixes the split.

Arjun (SE): Workarounds ranked: (A) For demo: force websocket fallback in SDK (`transport: 'websocket'`) — no infra change for hosted. (B) If they can't use ws, implement client-side reassembly: buffer parts keyed by id and only JSON.parse when whole payload assembled (brace balancing or id marker). (C) Upgrade SDK to `@redwood/web-sdk@1.4.2` which includes incremental UTF-8 buffering.

Claire (Client Eng): Can you send a tiny reassembly snippet and websocket toggle?

Arjun (SE): Snippets: websocket: `const c = new RedwoodClient({ transport: 'websocket', token: '...' })`. Reassembly (very small):
```
const buf = {};
es.addEventListener('message', e => {
  const p = JSON.parse(e.data); // assume meta always complete
  buf[p.id] = (buf[p.id] || '') + p.part;
  try { const full = JSON.parse(buf[p.id]); handle(full); delete buf[p.id]; } catch(e){ /* keep buffering */ }
});
```
This is a POC workaround only.

deploy-bot: Deployed stream-utf8-patch v2027.01.18 by @arjun  includes web-sdk 1.4.2 with improved incremental UTF-8 handling.

Mia (Sales): I'll propose websocket fallback for the live walkthrough and ask Claire to try the buffer snippet if they can't change the proxy. Claire, please share HAR + `curl -N -v` output and I'll coordinate. Thanks team :thumbsup:
